trust_decision.summary: Which client IP keys the per-IP rate-limit bucket and the auth audit log; decided inline from the first X-Forwarded-For element, falling back to remote_addr, in three copied expressions. The CNL loopback check is coupled because the fix's ProxyFix rewrites remote_addr.

landing_point.why: The advisory title says rate-limit bypass, and rate_limit() is the only rate limiter. Its inline XFF expression is the obvious first hit, and grepping 'X-Forwarded-For' then shows the other two copies.

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: src/pyload/webui/app/blueprints/cnl_blueprint.py:33 and src/pyload/webui/app/helpers.py:299. The CNL loopback gate reads REMOTE_ADDR/remote_addr. Once a solver adds trusted-proxy middleware, that value becomes header-derived, so the gate must read the original peer (fix.diff:114, fix.diff:129, fix.diff:135-138).

O3_reason_to_dismiss: Click'N'Load never reads X-Forwarded-For, and is_loopback_request already rejects forwarded headers by default (src/pyload/webui/app/helpers.py:292-297). It is a separate feature on port 9666 and looks untouched by an XFF bug.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Two legitimate behaviours sit next to the sink. Reverse-proxy deployments still need the real client IP via a configured trusted-hop count; an over-broad fix that drops forwarded headers entirely breaks this, and the published fix keeps it via trusted_proxies (fix.diff:13, fix.diff:33-39). Local Click'N'Load from loopback must also keep returning 200 (tests/integration/test_cnl.py:10-23).
